title: Condemnation of Shah Nawaz and Lakhpat Rai

blocks.text: After the massacre, Shah Nawaz is presented as drunk on power and dreaming of a still higher station, while Lakhpat Rai shares in the same swollen arrogance. The page frames both men as rulers whose apparent success has already made them fit objects of divine judgment.

It then lingers on their anti-Sikh persecution in deliberate detail, stressing that the word Guru was forbidden, the name of Nanak was twisted into insult, and listeners to the Guru’s bani were pressured toward Islam by men who treated reverence itself as a crime.

The page also remembers desecration of scripture as part of the same campaign of contempt. By gathering these offenses together, the narrative prepares the complaint that heaven itself will answer in the pages that follow.
